radar.justification: Proprietary program with an unpublished Acceptance Framework; only Verifiable Intent is open.
Mastercard registers agents and issues tokens, as Visa does for TAP; Skyfire is a named Know Your Agent partner, and AP4M pilots settle on Base.
Network enablement in several regions but named transactions are pilots; developer docs an early preview.
Many named banks and partners, no volume data.
Tokens with limits and VI Autonomous mandates support delegation; VI not shown in live authorizations.
Card chargeback rights apply; no public agent-specific codes (Agent Pay Program Standards not public); VI evidence without liability rules.

controlsCells.note: Registered agents sign requests with RFC 9421 and the tag Agent-pay-auth; verifiers check against the Mastercard key directory at the CDN or merchant.
Registration, security review, certification and trusted agent lists; Skyfire named as Know Your Agent partner on 2026-09-30.
Consumer authorizes the agent and sets limits; passkeys in regional pilots; Verifiable Intent L2 signed by the user key.
Tokens limited by merchant, amount or time window; Verifiable Intent amount_range and budget constraints.
Merchant-specific tokens; Verifiable Intent allowed_merchants and allowed_payees; Intent API srcDpaId check.
Time-limited tokens, signature created and expires, orderExpiry, Verifiable Intent layer lifetimes (L3 at most one hour).

No public API to revoke an agent or an Agentic Token. MVCT tokens used by Agent Pay integrators can be deleted (Delete Card) and are suspended or cancelled by issuers, with notifications. Verifiable Intent 0.1 has no revocation protocol, only JWKS key removal and expiry.
Passkeys at consent; deferred orders escalated to the consumer; 3DS for agentic flows still in development at networks and EMVCo.
Mandatory nonce and short window on signatures; single-use tokens and one-time DTVC; Verifiable Intent nonce, aud and one L3 pair per mandate pair.
Verifiable Intent chain gives dispute evidence; intent records kept as chargeback evidence; no receipt object in the program.

Standard chargeback rights apply (Mastercard). No agent-specific reason code or liability rule is public: the Mastercard Rules (2026-06-02) require Agent Pay Program Standards that are not public, and Worldpay (2026-07-30) says no liability shift exists yet. Verifiable Intent leaves dispute choreography out of scope.
No public agent reputation score; the probability score rates transactions, not agents.

Mastercard aims to make agent transactions recognizable to issuers; a probability score for AI-initiated transactions is rolling out for US testing (announced 2026-09-30); Verifiable Intent risk_data at consent.
Issuers keep card-level blocks and declines; no documented control to disable one agent across the network.
